title: State of Maharashtra v. Ajmal Amir Kasab (26/11 Mumbai Terror Attacks)
crime_type: Waging War Against State / Mass Homicide / Maritime Infiltration / Terror Attack
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Bombay / Special Court Mumbai
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1965342)
ipc_sections: Section 121 IPC (Waging war against the Government of India)
location: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, Cama Hospital, Girgaum Chowpatty, Mumbai, India
evidence: Live apprehension at Girgaum Chowpatty barricade by Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble holding rifle barrel
Seizure of AK-47 assault rifle, 9mm pistols, hand grenades, RDX explosive timers, and satellite GPS receivers
CCTV footage from CST railway station depicting indiscriminate firing into passenger waiting halls
VoIP and Thuraya satellite phone intercepts capturing real-time tactical instructions from handlers in Karachi
DNA profiling matching deceased terrorists to hijacked fishing trawler MV Kuber
modus_operandi: Ten heavily armed terrorists hijacked an Indian fishing trawler, murdered the crew, and entered Mumbai coast via inflatable dinghies. Deployed in two-man buddy pairs targeting public transit hubs, luxury hotels, and hospitals with assault rifles and grenades to maximize civilian casualties and draw global media attention.
personality_disorder: Systematic religious radicalization, indoctrinated fanaticism, and ruthless sociopathic indifference to human life.
common_traits: Maritime cross-border infiltration via hijacked vessels
Assault rifles and military-grade hand grenades in crowded transit hubs
Hostage-taking and tactical standoff against elite commandos
Real-time tactical direction via VoIP satellite intercepts
summary: The 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks claimed 166 lives. The trial set international standards for digital and forensic evidence handling in mass terror prosecutions. Sole surviving terrorist Ajmal Kasab was convicted under Section 121 and 302 and executed in 2012.
